events.title: The Last Hohenstaufen King Is Executed
events.description: Conradin, the teenage claimant to the Kingdom of Sicily and the last legitimate male heir of the Hohenstaufen dynasty, was executed in Naples after his defeat by Charles of Anjou.
events.significance: His death ended the Hohenstaufen line, which had dominated medieval Germany and Italy, and cemented Angevin power in southern Italy.

events.title: Leibniz Introduces the Integral Sign
events.description: The German polymath Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz used the elongated 'S' symbol (∫) for the first time to represent the integral in his calculus notes.
events.significance: Leibniz's notation became the standard way of writing integrals and is still used in mathematics, physics and engineering today.

events.title: Black Tuesday Hits Wall Street
events.description: Investors traded more than 16 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange in a single day as prices collapsed, wiping out billions of dollars in value.
events.significance: The crash was a defining moment of the 1929 market collapse and a prelude to the Great Depression, which reshaped economic policy around the world.

events.title: The First Message Is Sent Over ARPANET
events.description: From a computer at UCLA, programmer Charley Kline sent the first electronic message to a machine at the Stanford Research Institute, linking two computers across a network.
events.significance: This early link on ARPANET, the forerunner of the internet, marked the start of networked computing as we know it.

events.title: Turkey Becomes a Republic
events.description: The Grand National Assembly proclaimed the Republic of Turkey, and Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was elected as its first president.
events.significance: The proclamation closed the Ottoman era and began a sweeping program of modernization and secularization. Turkey still celebrates it each year as Republic Day.
